function: Excluded (system), p. 4: DQN and SAC adjust the 5G NR PRS frame (subcarrier spacing, sensing-slot ratio) and schedule downlink tasks for ISAC over a scalar single-antenna link without RIS.
notes: Exclusion code system, shown on p. 4. The PDF is the paper of the DOI (title and DOI on p. 1). Codes 1-5 do not apply: research article; DRL agents (DQN for frame adjustment, SAC for task scheduling, pp. 9-10) choose the NR subcarrier spacing and the ratio of PRS sensing slots (p. 7, Eq. (26)), a waveform and sensing/communication resource decision of area 5 (ISAC), learned jointly with packet scheduling, so above_phy does not apply. The link is single-antenna with no RIS: p. 4: "the double-trip time-varying channel response corresponding to the pth user can be represented as hp(t, τ) = ξp e^{j2πνp t} δ(t − τp)", and the received signal of Eq. (6), "yu(t) = ξp xu(t − 2rp/c) e^{j2πνp t} + n(t)", is scalar; the communication SNR is scalar too, p. 5: "γ^p_{m,u} = p_{m,u}|ϱp|^2/σn^2"; Table IV (p. 11) lists no antenna number, array, or RIS, and sensing estimates only range and velocity, not angle (pp. 4-5). The paper never mentions antennas, MIMO, arrays, or beamforming in its own system; "beam scanning time" appears only as a reason to fix the PRS mapping (p. 4). It does report simulation results (pp. 11-14; 27.5 GHz, Table IV p. 11). For the reviewer: the antenna count is not stated, the single-antenna reading rests on the scalar model; if the frame adjustment were judged above the physical layer, the code would be above_phy instead (pp. 7-8).
